newsitem.title: USA: US Prudential Insurance says open to Florida talks.
newsitem.headline: US Prudential Insurance says open to Florida talks.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America said on Monday that it is open to talks with Florida officials about allegations of deceptive sales practices by its agents.
Florida Insurance Commissioner Bill Nelson earlier today accused the insurance company of obstructing a state probe into allegations that the company had misrepresented its insurance products.

Prudential said it has entered agreements with 46 states about the sales practices that misled customers to believe they were buying investments instead of insurance products and is anxious to begin its remediation program in Florida.
Nelson's office started an investigation in 1995 into the sales allegations that may involve 100,000 policy holders in Florida, Nelson said.
He also threatened to suspend Prudential's license if they are unable to provide documents involved with the investigation.
Prudential said the plan allows people who were misled to receive a settlement specific to their circumstances.
The remediation plan does not have a limit to the number of people who can receive the remedies or the amount of money Prudential would spend to provide the remedies, the company said.
Prudential said it has provided thousands of records and hundreds of witnesses for the inquiries.
A Prudential spokesman said the company provided for a $410 million minimum guarantee for the settlement for policyholders.

Non-commissioned employees will be calling insurance applicants after an agent visits a home to prevent future misrepresentations, the spokesman said. The non-commissioned employee will review the application and review how the insurance policy will be paid for and the amount of insurance.
One of the allegations levied against the company was that agents would borrow money from or surrender existing insurance policies to pay for new policies, officials said.
